title: Rural Home Loans Principal Paydown to the Escrow Waiver Limit — Member Handover Card
content:
A member of the Rural Home Loans program may make a principal paydown, by a one-time debit of the member's own account, so that the loan meets the escrow waiver loan-to-value limit; the paydown is booked as an extra principal payment and changes neither the monthly payment nor the next due date.

## What the paydown does

The member authorises a one-time debit of their own account for the amount given, which is booked today as an extra principal payment (curtailment) on the loan. The principal balance falls by that amount at once; the monthly payment and the next due date do not change, and the payment shows in the payment history as an extra principal payment. A paydown so booked is posted to the loan.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `make_principal_paydown_d2fdfc16`, a tool the customer themselves runs: the agent unlocks it and hands it over to the member, who runs it to authorise the debit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_id` | the loan number of the Country Home loan, as the servicing agent reads it out from the loan record | identifier |
| `paydown_amount` | the extra principal being paid, as the agent states it | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive |

## Return

A dictionary receipt: `txn_id` (reference number of the extra principal payment, a string); `amount` (the paydown, USD to 2 decimal places); `principal_balance` (the principal after the paydown, USD to 2 decimal places); and `status` ("posted" when the paydown is on the loan).

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

On a principal balance of 251234.56, a paydown run with `paydown_amount` 11234.56 returns `amount` 11234.56, `principal_balance` 240000.00 and `status` "posted"; the next due date and the monthly payment are as before.
